svg.title: moe-service-handler data flow: requests split across the workers
svg.desc: 1 · Two prompts come in to the controller. 2 · It gives each request to a worker, both at the same time: A to m1, B to m4b. 3 · Each worker runs the whole model on its request: prefill. 4 · Each token comes back as soon as it is made, and goes straight to the client. 5 · Every second a ping goes out; the status comes back: memory, what it is doing. 6 · The workers end their requests (token limit or end of text) and are ready again. 7 · Prompt C asks A again: the controller's own cache answers it, no worker is used. If a worker hangs: it is marked stuck, with what it was on, and gets no new work. The workers never talk to each other.
svg.text: split = "requests" · each worker runs streammoe on the whole model · docs/request-split.md
The controller runs no model: it hands whole requests to the workers, both at once, and manages them.
1 · Two prompts come in to the controller
2 · It gives each request to a worker, both at the same time: A to m1, B to m4b
3 · Each worker runs the whole model on its request: prefill
4 · Each token comes back as soon as it is made, and goes straight to the client
5 · Every second a ping goes out; the status comes back: memory, what it is doing
6 · The workers end their requests (token limit or end of text) and are ready again
7 · Prompt C asks A again: the controller's own cache answers it, no worker is used
If a worker hangs: it is marked stuck, with what it was on, and gets no new work
Mac mini M4 · no model · ~140 MiB + cache ≤ 32 MiB

One answer runs at one Mac's speed; two workers serve two requests at once. The workers never talk to each other.
Link: one TCP connection per worker, both ways. Big messages go in 64 KiB chunks, so pings and tokens never wait.
A lost link: pings and TCP keep-alive notice it; the controller reconnects (0.5 s doubling to 10 s) and the worker waits.
Unified memory: RAM and GPU memory are the same. The workers' math runs on the GPU; the controller only uses the CPU.
